authorization_note: every command in that order is one this grant already authorizes. No operation is added, no unrelated state is repaired, and no Job is re-admitted -- none has been admitted yet. The stop happens with the stores empty and nothing executing.
bounded_correction_the_packet_needs: sections 5 and 6 must publish start -> stop -> create -> start for a fresh installation, and section 4 must publish the workspace_storage prerequisite.
headline: ordinary template `create` cannot be reached on a FRESH installation without starting and then stopping the deployment first. Neither order the packet could publish works on its own.
the_supported_order_this_execution_uses: mkdir the configured workspace_storage -- the pilot packet publishes this as 'Selection 2b', the accepted packet omits it (separate finding)
stop    -> releases the manager instance guard; nothing is running, no Job exists, no runtime to cease
create  -> takes the guard it needs

the_two_refusals.order: create BEFORE start (what the accepted packet publishes)
the_two_refusals.refusal: ContractRefusal: a read-only manager requires an existing regular store
the_two_refusals.why: job_manager._create opens the control store with ControlStore.open_readonly, and on a fresh install db/control.sqlite3 does not exist. The ONLY writable open in job_manager is _serve (line 1168); _submit, _create and _status all open read-only. So the control store is created by SERVING.

the_two_refusals.refusal: ContractRefusal: another manager is already active for workspace '…/state/workspaces', holding control store '…/db/control.sqlite3'; only one Host manager may be active for one workspace and database, so this start is a configuration error rather than a standby -- point this manager at its own database and workspace, or stop the active one first
the_two_refusals.why: create_template_job -> fresh_attempt_ports.held -> borrow_manager_instance -> hold_manager_instance takes an EXCLUSIVE flock on the workspace instance guard. The running `manager serve` holds it.

why_my_own_proof_never_hit_it: prove_capacity.py:_create opened the control store itself with ControlStore.open and closed it before calling create, and it never started the deployment. Both refusals need a real fresh install plus a real serve loop; no inert proof reaches either.
why_the_pilot_never_hit_this: the pilot packet's Selection 3 uses `manager … submit --document …`, which takes NO --control operand and never opens the control store. The template `create` path does take --control. So this is new with template creation and the pilot precedent does not cover it.
